results_seen_note: No Study 2R borrowing outcome has been computed or read; the 2R article list does not exist yet. Known before this addendum: the parameter audit (data/reports/parameter_register.md), including noise calibrations on 596 LibriVox book articles (interest only) and on 1,500 random Seattle works with random month 0 (no attention data), and the exploratory Study 3 dose-response of carry-over by shift duration and size (Study 3 outcomes, not 2R outcomes).

changes.events.minimum_volume: normal level at least 300 user views a week; the original 100 is kept only for the secondary sensitivity run
changes.events.ratio_rule: the rise ratio for single-book articles is set from interest data alone, on the final 2R article list, before any borrowing is computed: the smallest value in {1.5, 2.0, 2.5, 3.0, 4.0, 5.0} at which the noise share of sustained shifts is at most 0.30, the noise share being shifts per series-year in block-resampled series (each article's own quiet weeks, 8-week blocks, seed 20261014, as in code/parameter_audit/calibrate_book_series.py) divided by the same in the real series. If no value reaches 0.30, the value with the lowest noise share is used and the share is reported. The chosen value and its noise share are filed as a dated note in prereg/addenda_2r/ before outcomes are computed. Secondary sensitivities: ratio 1.5, and a noise-scaled ratio exp(6 x the article's MAD-based week-to-week SD of log share).
changes.inference.equivalence_anchor: 10% is the smallest lift of interest because it lies at the average carry-over of sustained category shifts in Study 3 (about 8 to 11% over months 0 to +2): a single-book effect smaller than the category average would not change the thesis's conclusion.
changes.inference.equivalence_feasibility: before outcomes are computed, the number of works a class needs for its upper 95% bound to fall below log(1.10) under a true effect of zero is computed from placebo windows on the 2R book list (random month 0, no attention data, method of code/parameter_audit/calibrate_2r_noise.py) and filed as a dated note. A class smaller than that is reported as inconclusive, with the largest lift ruled out, and receives no 'no meaningful effect' verdict.
changes.confirmatory.duration_threshold: Study 2R is the confirmatory test of the duration finding of the exploratory Study 3 dose-response. H1: pooled tau rises with the whole duration of the shift (slope of tau on log2 of duration in weeks above 0, bootstrap by work, 2,000 resamples, seed 20261013, one-sided at 0.05). H2: shifts lasting 6 weeks or more have higher tau than shifts lasting 1 or 2 weeks (difference above 0, 95% bootstrap interval above 0). Also reported, not tested: the coefficient of log2 peak size given log2 duration, and a Hansen (2000) threshold regression of tau on duration (candidate thresholds 2 to 10 weeks, bootstrap interval for the threshold). Whole duration is known only after a shift ends; it is used here because Study 2R explains past events and does not forecast.

reason: The parameter audit found that the category rule mostly detects ordinary variation on single-book articles (62% noise share for sustained shifts at ratio 1.5 and 100 views a week on a stand-in list), that the 10% bound had no written rationale and may be out of reach for small classes, and that in Study 3 carry-over grows with duration rather than stepping at 4 weeks. The Study 3 analysis that found this used all years, so held-out years of Study 3 can no longer confirm it; Study 2R outcomes are unseen and become the confirmation.
